notes.decision: Translated 'I have committed (it) to the hand of you all.' The verbal form ⲁϩ̄ⲧ (with overstroke) appears to be a Lycopolitan perfect-1sg form on a stem of placing/entrusting; combined with the idiom ⲁⲧⲟⲟⲧ⸗ 'into the hand of (someone)' attested elsewhere in the corpus for committing/enjoining (cf. ⲡⲉ†ϩⲱⲛ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁϥ ⲁⲧⲟⲧⲧⲏⲛⲉ in glossary), this gives a sense of formal apostolic entrustment of the catechumens with their soteriological responsibility.

Tentatively rendered 'a concealment'/'a hidden state'. The form ϩⲱⲯ is unusual; possibly Lyc reflex of ϩⲱⲡ 'be hidden, hide' substantivized. Alternative: a form of ⲱⲡ 'reckon, count' giving 'in a reckoning unto the end.' Confidence low.

The 3rd-person prefixes ⲁⲩ- could be either 3pl 'they (his fellow catechumens) blessed/worshipped/glorified' or 3sg.m 'he blessed/worshipped/glorified.' Given that the subject is a single catechumen who heard and responded, I render as 3sg.m ('he'). The Lycopolitan ⲁⲩ- can stand for either.

Treated as the chapter number 115 (ⲣ̄=100 + ⲓⲉ̄=15). Appears three times in lines 20-22 around the chapter title in an ornamental triple-marking pattern (opener, mid-title, closer), interrupting the textual flow. Preserved in the Coptic field but rendered as numeric marker '(115)' in English to flag its non-textual function. The recurrence inside line 22 (between ⲙⲁ- and -ⲣⲉ of the negative habitual ⲙⲁⲣⲉ) confirms it is a marginal/decorative element rather than a part of the prose.

The character ⲯ functions consistently for ϣ throughout this kephalaion's title and body (lines 21-33). This is a scribal/orthographic feature distinctive to this section. Translated normally as ϣ-forms: ⲯⲁⲛⲯⲱⲱⲧ = ϣⲁⲛϣⲱⲱⲧ 'when they cut'; ⲯⲱⲛⲉ = ϣⲱⲛⲉ 'be sick/pained'; ⲯⲁⲩⲧⲕⲉⲥ = ϣⲁⲩ-ⲧⲕⲉⲥ 'they habitually pain him' (with ⲧⲕⲉⲥ = ⲧⲕⲁⲥ 'pain, sting' per glossary).

Rendered 'the tip of the head.' ⲡϫⲁⲕ = 'tip, end, peak' (from ϫⲱⲕ 'complete' or ϫⲁⲕ 'edge'); ⲛⲧⲁⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲡⲉ is parsed as a Lycopolitan/scribal form of ⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲡⲉ 'of the head' with anomalous ⲛⲧⲁⲛ̄- prefix (possibly a reduplicated genitive marker). Given the context (cutting things on the head and feet without pain), this most plausibly designates the hair on top of the head — what is shaved (ⲯⲱⲃ = ϣⲱⲃ/ϣⲱⲱⲃ?) without causing pain.
